It assumes: OB clearance for moderate exercise, no jumping for 4 more weeks, home setup with light dumbbells (e.g., 2–8 kg), bands optional. Focus: rebuild core and pelvic floor function, reintroduce strength patterns, gradually progress load/volume/complexity, and manage fatigue. Week 1 is an acclimatisation/on-ramp—shorter, lower volume and RPE. All sessions are written 30–40 minutes unless noted.

Global guidelines
- Frequency: 3 strength-focused sessions/week + optional low-intensity cardio/mobility (1–2x).
- Intensity: RPE 4–6 most sets; leave 2–3 reps in reserve. Stop any drill that provokes pelvic heaviness/pressure, pain, or urinary leakage.
- Breathing/pressure: Exhale on exertion; avoid prolonged breath holds and heavy bracing. Progress from exhale-to-exert to gentle anticipatory brace as tolerated.
- Core/pelvic floor: Include daily 5–8 minutes of breath + pelvic floor coordination (see below).
- Tempo/control: Prioritize slow eccentrics (2–3s down) and full control, especially in single-leg and trunk work.
- No jumping/running. Use marches, step-ups, low-step power patterns without impact.

- 3D breathing: Crocodile or 90/90 breathing with pelvic floor connection, 5 breaths x 2–3 sets. Inhale to ribs/back; on exhale, lightly lift pelvic floor (like stopping gas/urine) at the end of the breath, then fully release on next inhale.
- Gentle mobility: Cat-cow x 6, open books x 6/side, ankle rocks x 10, hip flexor glide x 5/side with glute squeeze.

You can do a simple, repeatable screen in-session to monitor both the width and—more importantly—tension/functional control of the linea alba as she progresses. Use the same setup, cues, and timing each time so changes are meaningful. If anything is unclear or concerning, refer to a pelvic health PT for formal assessment.

When to screen
- Baseline: before starting the block.
- Checkpoints: end of Week 2 and end of Week 4, or sooner if she reports coning, midline pain, or new bulge/heaviness.
- Also spot-check during new/progressive drills (e.g., dead bugs, planks, RDLs) if form or pressure strategy shifts.

What you’re looking for
- Width: the distance between rectus edges (in finger widths) at the umbilicus, 2 cm above, and 2 cm below.
- Depth/tension: how the midline feels when she lightly lifts her head/shoulders—does it firm up under your fingers or feel soft/sinky? Can she create tension with exhale and gentle brace?
- Appearance under load: any doming/coning along the midline, bulging at the navel, or “valley” collapse when she exerts.
- Symptoms: pain along the linea alba, back pain linked to core tasks, pelvic floor symptoms (heaviness, leakage) during core work.

Simple palpation screen (trainer- or self-check)
1) Position
- Have her lie supine, knees bent, feet flat, head supported. Ensure bladder reasonably empty and she’s relaxed.
- Your hand position: fingers flat and together, pointing toward her head.

2) At rest
- Place fingertips at the umbilicus. Gently press down until you meet the abdominal wall.
- Note baseline tone and any visible doming/valley.

3) Head lift without breath cue
- Ask her to slowly lift head/shoulders just until shoulder blades start to clear. Do not cue breathing yet.
- Feel for the gap width (how many finger widths fit) and depth (how far fingers sink) and whether tissue firms.
- Repeat 2 cm above and 2 cm below the navel.

4) Head lift with pressure strategy
- Repeat the lift, but this time cue: exhale, gently draw ribs down, light pelvic floor lift, then lift head. Reassess width and tension.
- A “good” response is improved tension (firmer trampoline-like feel) and/or slight narrowing with the strategy.

5) Loaded look test
- In hook-lying, have her do 4–5 reps each: heel slides, dead bug arm lowers, gentle bridge, and a small cough. Watch for coning/doming.
- If coning appears, pause and regress lever length or load; note which drill provoked it.

How to record
- Use the same three sites (above/at/below umbilicus).
- Note width in finger widths (e.g., 2.0 above, 1.5 at, 1.0 below).
- Note depth/tension: firm/elastic vs soft/sinky; whether strategy improved tension.
- Note any coning and the drill that triggered it, plus what regression resolved it.

Interpreting findings
- Common/functional: A gap up to about 2 finger widths that firms with exhale/brace, no symptomatic coning in daily tasks. Train as planned, keep pressure strategy cues.
- Monitor closely: 2–3+ finger widths and/or tissue that remains soft/sinky with load, intermittent coning in exercise. Continue training with regressions (shorter levers, more support), emphasize breath/bracing, avoid straining.
- Refer/modify: Persistent coning at low loads, inability to generate tension, pain along the midline, or associated pelvic floor symptoms. Recommend pelvic health PT for individualized strategies.

Exercise-specific observation checklist
- Squat and hinge: watch for rib flare, breath holding, or doming on ascent. Cue exhale on exertion, “zip up” lightly, and reduce load/ROM if needed.
- Push-up/planks: monitor along the whole line from sternum to below navel. Elevate hands or shorten hold if doming.
- Dead bugs/bear hovers: prioritize shorter levers; if coning appears, bend knees more, reduce reach, slow the tempo, or return to isometrics.
- Carries: look for excessive rib flare/overextension. Cue tall posture, soft ribs.

Progression rules tied to the screen
- Progress when she can perform the current variation with: no visible coning, steady breathing (no valsalva), and a firmer midline feel under light load.
- If coning or soft/sinky response persists, hold or regress the variation and build time under tension first, then range, then load.
- Re-test the quick palpation after introducing a new, more challenging lever (e.g., moving from knees-bent dead bug to heel taps).

Communication and education points
- Explain that diastasis is common postpartum and the goal is functional tension and symptom-free movement, not “zero gap.”
- Encourage her to self-check visually during movements and to stop/adjust if she notices coning or pressure.
- Track photos or short videos (side and top views) during core drills at each checkpoint to compare control over time.

Red flags warranting referral
- Increasing gap with worsening tension over several weeks.
- Pain along the linea alba, bulging hernia suspicion, or non-resolving coning in daily life tasks.
- Pelvic floor red flags: heaviness/dragging, leakage that is new/worsening, or vaginal pressure with light activity.

This framework lets you monitor diastasis functionally while keeping training productive and safe, and it gives you clear decision points for progression or referral.

We can, however, use “HIIT‑lite” formats that deliver a strong training effect without impact, breath‑holding, or heavy bracing. These will scratch the HIIT itch and support fat loss while we build capacity for true HIIT after clearance.

Principles
- Keep it seated or low-impact, RPE peaks ≤7 for now.
- Intervals short/moderate with full, easy recovery.
- No jumping/running/standing hill sprints; no breath holds.
- Stop if pelvic heaviness, leakage, coning, sharp pain, or increased lochia.

Where it fits
- 1–2 sessions/week on nonconsecutive days.
- Place ≥24 hours away from the heaviest lower-body strength day.
- Keep total session time 20–30 minutes. If sleep is poor or she’s run-down, swap to steady state.

Options to use now (HIIT‑lite)

1) Seated spin intervals (primary)
- Warm-up: 8 minutes very easy, include 3 x 20s gentle cadence pick-ups (RPE 5).
- Main set: 6–8 rounds of 60s at RPE 6–7 (seated, moderate resistance, smooth cadence 80–95 RPM) followed by 90–120s easy spin at RPE 3–4.
- Cool-down: 5–8 minutes very easy.
- Pelvic floor cue: gentle exhale at start of each surge; if pressure felt, reduce resistance and stay truly seated/upright.

2) Sub‑max spin “floats”
- Warm-up 6–8 min easy.
- Main: 3–4 x 5 minutes at RPE 6 (seated) with 3 minutes easy between.
- Cool-down 5–6 min.
- This is more tempo than HIIT but gives a strong metabolic hit without spikes.

3) Low-impact “metcon” circuit (no impact)
Perform 4–5 rounds, work 40s, rest 20–30s between stations; 2–3 minutes easy walk between rounds.
- Low step-ups (20–25 cm), alternate legs, slow control.
- Suitcase carry walk (moderate DB), out-and-back.
- Band row or chest-supported DB row (light–moderate).
- Marching with high arms or light DB overhead hold (keep ribs stacked).
Keep RPE ≤7. If breath gets ragged or pressure builds, extend rest.

4) Row erg (only if she’s experienced and symptom-free)
- 8 min easy → 8–10 x 45s at RPE 6–7 / 75–90s very easy → 5–6 min cool-down.
- Technique: exhale on the drive, no yanking or max strokes.

Progression across the next 4 weeks
- Week 1 of HIIT-lite: 1 session, choose Option 1, 6 rounds cap, RPE peaks ≤6.5.
- Week 2: 1–2 sessions. Option 1 to 7–8 rounds, or add Option 3 for variety (4 rounds).
- Week 3: 2 sessions max. Keep seated spin intervals; you can shorten recovery a touch (e.g., 60s on / 75–90s easy) if zero symptoms.
- Week 4: Maintain 2 sessions but do not increase peak intensity; instead, add 1 more round or 1–2 minutes to tempo portions.

Fat loss notes (expectation setting)
- Nutrition drives the majority of fat loss. Keep protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day, eat mostly whole foods, and aim for a modest calorie deficit only if energy, milk supply (if breastfeeding), and recovery remain good. HIIT-lite helps with expenditure and fitness but shouldn’t replace strength or sleep.
- If breastfeeding, avoid aggressive deficits; prioritize hydration and carbohydrates around training.

Green/Yellow/Red check on every interval day
- Green: breathing controlled (no valsalva), no pelvic symptoms, no coning—proceed.
- Yellow: mild heaviness/pressure or back tightness—drop intensity to RPE 5–6, extend recovery, or switch to steady state.
- Red: leakage, sharp pain, visible coning/bulge, or increased lochia—stop intervals, do easy spin/walk only, and reassess next session.

When true HIIT can return
- After the no-jump window lifts, and if she passes a hop/impact prep screen (e.g., 30s pogos holds, quick step switches, single-leg balance with no symptoms), you can trial short standing climbs on the bike (20–30s, RPE 7–7.5, 2–3 reps) and progress gradually toward higher-intensity efforts. Introduce running/jump intervals only after a separate, graded return-to-impact phase is symptom-free.

This slots satisfying, safe interval work into her plan now, supports fat loss, and preserves the long game of pelvic floor and core health.

  - Calf raises single‑leg x 20/side controlled.
- Core/pressure: no coning in dead bugs, planks (elevated), or push‑ups; can exhale/brace on exertion.
- Impact prep screen (performed on a good energy day)
  - 30s each: in‑place marching, fast marching, low step quick switches (10–15 cm), and pogo position holds (ankles stiff, no bouncing) — zero symptoms.
  - Single‑leg balance eyes forward 30s/side without hip drop or wobble.
  - Optional: 10–15 small double‑leg heel pops (minimal lift, “quiet landings”) symptom‑free.

If any of the above provoke symptoms, stay with impact prep and re‑test in 1–2 weeks; consider pelvic health PT if symptoms persist.

Timeline and progression overview
- Weeks 12–16 postpartum: finish the current on‑ramp, build walking volume to 40–60 min, add impact prep 2–3x/week. If all green, start run‑walk.
- Weeks 16–20: graded run‑walk progression 2–3x/week on flat terrain.
- Weeks 20+ (summer): transition to continuous runs, layer one quality session/week, maintain 2 strength days.
- 8–10 weeks out from the autumn 10k: add race‑specific volume, light tempos, and strides (if fully symptom‑free).

Run‑walk ramp (example, 3 runs/week max, 48h between run days)
- Session format each day: 5–8 min brisk walk warm‑up → mobility (ankle/hip) 1–2 min → run‑walk sets → 5–8 min easy walk cool‑down + light calves/hips.
- Keep all running at easy conversational pace. If HR or breath surges, slow to a shuffle before walking.

Week 1 (first week of running)
- A: 8 x 1 min run / 1.5–2 min walk (≈20–24 min work)
- B: 6 x 1.5 min run / 2 min walk
- C: 10 x 1 min run / 1.5 min walk
Stop early if any pelvic heaviness, leakage, sharp pain, or abdominal coning.

Week 2
- A: 6 x 2 min run / 2 min walk
- B: 5 x 3 min run / 2 min walk
- C: 8 x 2 min run / 90s walk

Week 3
- A: 4 x 5 min run / 2 min walk
- B: 3 x 8 min run / 3 min walk
- C: 20 min continuous run test if A and B were symptom‑free; otherwise repeat B.

Week 4
- Two continuous easy runs 20–25 min + one run‑walk filler (e.g., 3 x 8 min run / 2 min walk).
- Total weekly run time target: 60–75 min easy.

Rules of progression and red flags
- 10–15% rule: increase total weekly run time or the longest run by no more than ~10–15% per week.
- Only progress a variable if the last two runs were symptom‑free during and 24–48 hours after.
- If symptoms appear: stop the session, walk home, and in the next run regress 1–2 steps (shorter run intervals or more walk). Add extra pelvic floor/core prep that week.
- Post‑run checklist: no leakage, no heaviness, no increase in lochia, no sharp pelvic/low‑back pain during or after, no prolonged DOMS in pelvic floor or hip flexors.

Strength and prep to support running (2x/week minimum)
- Keep hinges, squats, split squats, step‑ups, calf work, and anti‑rotation core.
- Add: 
  - Calf raises heavy (bent‑ and straight‑knee) 3 x 12–15.
  - Lateral hip work (banded walks, side‑lying abduction) 2–3 sets.
  - Low‑level plyo prep once cleared: pogo holds → small pogos → low step quick pops, 2x/week, 5–8 min.

Surface, footwear, and terrain
- Start on flat, forgiving surfaces (track outer lanes, smooth park paths, treadmill).
- Avoid cambered roads and downhills early on.
- Replace worn shoes; consider mild stability if she had pregnancy‑related pronation changes.

Building toward a 10k (once running continuously 25–30 min)
- Frequency: 3 runs/week.
  - Easy run: 30–45 min.
  - Long run: build from 35–40 min to 60–70 min over 6–8 weeks.
  - Quality day (introduced only when fully symptom‑free): light tempo or cruise intervals, e.g., 3 x 6–8 min at “comfortably hard” with 2–3 min easy jog, or 6–8 x 30s relaxed strides with full recovery.
- Cutback every 3–4 weeks (reduce volume by ~20–30%) to consolidate.

When to refer
- Persistent leakage, heaviness, pain, or visible doming with low‑impact running, or if progress stalls despite regressions—refer to a pelvic health physiotherapist for tailored strategies.

Bottom line
- Eager runners can usually start a careful run‑walk around 12–16 weeks postpartum if all screens are green. With steady, symptom‑led progression, she can be comfortably preparing for an autumn 10k while keeping pelvic floor and core health front and center.

Here’s the full 4-week return-to-fitness on-ramp re-issued with all adjustments layered in: added cardio (including HIIT-lite), the anti-flexion core track, screening/guardrails for diastasis, and the “push” intensity pathway starting mid–Week 2. Assumptions: 10–14 weeks postpartum, OB cleared for moderate exercise, no jumping for 4 more weeks, home setup with light dumbbells/bands. Week 1 is acclimatisation.

Global guidelines
- Frequency targets per week:
  - Strength: 3 sessions
  - Cardio: 2–4 sessions (mix of steady spin/walk and HIIT-lite 1–2x max)
  - Core add-on: 3–4 mini-sessions (8–12 minutes), placed after strength or cardio
  - Impact: none (no running/jumping yet)
- Intensity: most strength work RPE 5–6 (can touch 6–7 on top sets from mid–Week 2). Cardio mostly RPE 4–6; HIIT-lite peaks ≤7.
- Breathing/pressure: exhale on exertion; avoid breath holding. If pelvic heaviness/pressure, leakage, lochia increase, midline coning, or sharp pain, reduce or stop and regress.
- Daily micro (5–8 min all weeks): 3D breathing + pelvic floor connection (5 breaths x 2–3), cat-cow x 6, open books x 6/side, ankle rocks x 10, half-kneeling hip flexor glide x 5/side with glute squeeze.

Screening and monitoring
- Diastasis quick screen: baseline before Week 1, re-check end of Week 2 and Week 4, and spot-check when progressing levers. Track width (finger widths) above/at/below umbilicus, and tension change with exhale/brace. Regress any drill that provokes coning or a soft/sinky response under load.
- Pelvic floor red flags: heaviness/dragging, leakage, increased lochia, pelvic/lumbar pain. If any appear, cut intensity/volume 25–50% that day and retest next session; refer to pelvic health PT if persistent.

Warm-up template (5–7 min before strength or circuits)
- 1–2 min easy march or low step
- T-spine rotation x 6/side
- 10 bodyweight sit-to-stands
- 8 hip hinge wall taps
- 8 wall scap slides

WEEK 1: Acclimatisation (3 strength sessions; 25–35 min; RPE 4–5)
Goal: Rehearse patterns, reconnect breath/core, assess tolerance. Cardio light and seated/low-impact. Core short and supported.

Strength Session A
- Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch with posterior tilt: 30s/side x 2
- Pelvic floor + breath in hook-lying with heel slides: 6–8/side x 2
- Sit-to-stand to high box (BW): 8–10 x 2; 2–3s down
- Incline push-up (hands on counter): 6–8 x 2
- Hip hinge to wall (BW): 8–10 x 2
- Bear hover regress (knees 1–2 cm) on exhales: 5 breaths x 2
- Farmer carry march (very light DBs): 20–30s x 2

Strength Session B
- 90/90 breathing + light band pull-apart: 8 breaths x 2
- Supported split squat (hands to chair as needed): 6/side x 2
- One-arm DB row (supported): 8/side x 2
- Glute bridge (BW, mini pause): 8–10 x 2
- Dead bug arms-only (feet down): 6–8/side x 2
- Tall-kneeling Pallof press (light band): 8/side x 2

Strength Session C
- Low step-up (20–25 cm), slow control: 6/side x 2
- Standing overhead press (very light DBs or band): 6–8 x 2
- RDL pattern with dowel/light DBs: 8 x 2
- Side-lying clamshell: 10/side x 2
- Side plank from knees: 15–20s/side x 2
- Seated calf raise (BW): 10–12 x 2

Cardio Week 1 (pick 2–3)
- Spin/walk steady only, RPE 4–5, 15–25 min.
- Spin example: 5 min easy → 3 x 3 min easy–moderate (RPE 5) with 2 min easy → 5 min cool-down. All seated.

Anti-flexion core add-on Week 1 (2–3x, 8–10 min)
- Dead bug isometric (legs tabletop): 4 x 15–20s with slow exhales (option: hand-to-thigh press)
- Side plank from knees: 2 x 15–20s/side
- Tall-kneeling Pallof press: 2 x 8–10/side (2s hold)
- Quadruped hover regress: 2 x 10–15s
- Optional suitcase hold: 2 x 20–30s/side

WEEK 2: Build base, begin “push” mid-week if green (3 strength sessions; 30–40 min; RPE 5–6, optional top sets ~6–7)
Goal: Slight load/volume bump; introduce light progressions. Start “push” pathway from Session B if symptom-free.

Strength Session A
- Glute bridge with band at knees: 10–12 x 3
- Goblet box squat (light DB): 8–10 x 3
- Incline push-up (slightly lower if clean): 8–10 x 3
- One-arm DB row: 8–10/side x 3
- Dead bug (tabletop with alternating heel taps short lever): 5–6/side x 2
- Farmer carry march: 30–40s x 2–3

Strength Session B (begin push if all green)
- Split squat (light support) → progress to light goblet: 3 x 8–10/side
- DB RDL (2 DBs), 3s eccentric: 3 x 10 (add small load if clean)
- Half-kneeling single-arm press: 8/side x 3
- Tall-kneeling band pulldown or lat prayer: 10–12 x 3
- Pallof press standing: 10/side x 2–3
- Heel-elevated calf raise: 12–15 x 2

Strength Session C (push path continued if green)
- Low step-up with 3s eccentric: 3 x 8–10/side
- Chest-supported DB row: 10 x 3
- Hinge rhythm patterning (no swing): 8 x 2
- Side-lying hip abduction: 10/side x 2–3
- Side plank from knees with top-leg straight: 15–25s/side x 2
- Bird dog (short lever): 6/side x 2

Cardio Week 2
- 3 sessions, 20–30 min.
- Spin: 5 min easy → 4 x 3 min RPE 5–6 seated with 2 min easy → 5 min cool-down.
- Walk: 20–30 min flat/moderate.
- HIIT-lite (add 1 session this week if eager, peaks ≤6.5): Seated spin 60s at RPE 6–6.5 / 90–120s easy x 6 rounds after 8-min warm-up; 5–6 min cool-down.

Anti-flexion core add-on Week 2 (3x, 8–10 min)
- Dead bug contralateral reach (short lever): 2–3 x 5–6/side, 2s pause
- Side plank from knees with top-leg straight: 2 x 20–25s/side
- Standing Pallof press: 2–3 x 8–10/side (add mini step-out on last reps)
- Bear hover holds: 2–3 x 12–20s
- Suitcase carry march: 2 x 30–40s/side or 20–30m/side

WEEK 3: Progressive strength and single-leg control, “push” pathway (3 strength sessions; 35–40 min; RPE up to 6–7 on top sets)
Goal: Add load or reps; more unilateral stability; maintain zero-impact. Cardio includes stronger seated intervals.

Strength Session A
- Goblet squat (to free depth or lower box): 3 x 10–12; last set RPE ~7 if clean
- DB RDL (2 DBs): 3 x 8–10; 3s down + 1s pause at shins; add load if brace clean
- Push-up progression (lowest controlled incline): 3 x 10–12
- One-arm DB row: 3 x 12/side; 1–2s squeeze at top
- Dead bug contralateral reach: 2–3 x 6–8/side
- Suitcase carry: 2 x 30–40m/side

Strength Session B
- Rear-foot supported split squat (rear toes on floor/low pad) with light–moderate goblet: 3 x 8–10/side
- Standing single-arm press: 3 x 8–10/side
- Banded hinge (pull-through or good morning): 3 x 12
- Tall-kneeling face pull (band): 3 x 12–15
- Side plank, top-leg straight: 2 x 25–30s/side
- Pallof step-out: 2 x 8–10/side

Strength Session C
- Step-up (slightly higher if pristine): 3 x 8–10/side, 2–3s down
- Bridge march (pause at top): 3 x 8–10/side
- Chest-supported reverse fly: 3 x 12
- Single-leg calf raise (supported, with DB): 3 x 10–12/side
- Bird dog full: 2 x 8/side
- 4–5 min mobility finisher

Cardio Week 3
- Spin session 1 (tempo blocks): 6 min easy → 3 x 5 min at RPE 6 (seated) with 3 min easy → 5–6 min cool-down (≈30–33 min).
- Spin session 2 (HIIT-lite): 8 min easy with 3 x 20s pick-ups → 6–8 x 60s at RPE 6–7 (seated, 80–95 RPM, moderate resistance) / 90–120s easy → 5–8 min cool-down.
- Optional third steady session: 25–30 min at RPE 5–6.
- Walking can replace or add easy volume 20–30 min on non-strength days.

Anti-flexion core add-on Week 3 (3x, 9–12 min)
- Dead bug with mini band overhead (light pull on exhale): 2–3 x 6–8/side
- Side plank staggered (bottom knee down, top foot planted): 2 x 20–30s/side
- Half-kneeling anti-flexion pressout (hold DB at chest, press out with 2s hold): 2–3 x 8/side
- Bear crawl iso (opposite hand/knee lift 1–2 cm; alternate): 2 x 6–8 slow switches/side
- Offset farmer carry: 2 x 45–60s total, switch at halfway

WEEK 4: Consolidate and prep next phase (3 strength sessions; 35–40 min; RPE 6–7 on top sets)
Goal: Solidify movement quality, small intensity bump, and test tolerance for next block. Still no impact. Intervals stay seated.

Strength Session A
- Goblet squat: 3 x 10–12; add one top set RPE ~7–7.5, then one back-off set (-2 reps)
- DB RDL: 3 x 8–10 heavier; 3s down, slight pause at shins
- Push-up progression: 3 x 10–12 at lowest clean incline
- One-arm DB row: 3 x 12/side; last set AMRAP to technical RPE 8 (leave 2 reps in reserve)
- Dead bug with banded exhale: 2–3 x 6–8/side
- Suitcase carry continuous: 2 x 45–60s total, switch halfway

Strength Session B
- Split squat (moderate goblet): 3 x 10/side
- Hip hinge pulse set: DB RDL to mid-shin + 1–2 “float” pulses each rep: 3 x 8
- Standing single-arm press: 3 x 10/side; final set RPE ~7
- Band pulldown → pull-apart superset: 2–3 rounds of 10 + 12
- Side plank top-leg lift (from knees): 2 x 20–25s/side
- Pallof iso-hold: 2 x 20–25s/side

Strength Session C
- Step-up (highest safe), slow eccentric: 3 x 10/side
- Feet-elevated bridge on low step (add DB on hips if clean): 3 x 8–10
- Chest-supported row + reverse fly combo: 3 x (8 + 10)
- Single-leg calf raise (supported): 3 x 12/side
- Quadruped hover shoulder taps (small range): 2 x 6–8/side
- Finisher: 5–7 min continuous alternating 30s march / 30s suitcase hold (switch sides each round)

Cardio Week 4
- Spin steady day: 10 min easy → 15–20 min continuous RPE 5–6 seated → 5–10 min cool-down (30–40 min total).
- Spin interval day (HIIT-lite): 6–8 min easy → 6 x 2 min at RPE 6–6.5 (seated) with 2 min easy → 6–8 min cool-down.
- Optional third session: 30–40 min walk, mostly flat.
- Keep peaks ≤7; extend duration or add a round rather than increasing intensity.

Anti-flexion core add-on Week 4 (3–4x, 10–12 min)
- Dead bug with heel taps (maintain lumbar neutral): 2–3 x 6–8/side; if coning, revert to Week 3 version
- Side plank from feet supported (top foot in front or knees slightly bent): 2 x 20–30s/side
- Pallof press iso-hold then reps: 2 x 20–25s/side then 6–8 slow presses/side
- Quadruped hover shoulder taps: 2 x 6–8/side
- Suitcase carry continuous: 2 x 45–60s total, switch halfway

Readiness gates and regressions
- Progress a variable (load, reps, ROM, tempo, density, or stability) only if the last session’s variation was symptom‑free and diastasis check shows good tension with exhale/brace.
- If any red flag appears mid-set, stop, reduce ROM/load, elevate support, and coach exhale-to-exert. Retest a lighter version; if still symptomatic, remove that drill for the day.

Nutrition and recovery (non-clinical guidance)
- Protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day across 3–4 meals. Include a protein serving within 1–2 hours post-session.
- Carbs to support energy and milk production if breastfeeding; include a pre-training snack if under-fueled.
- Hydration 2–3 L/day; +500–700 mL around training; more if breastfeeding.
- Sleep: prioritize consistency and naps; if fatigue ≥7/10, reduce day’s volume by 20–30%.

Return-to-running outlook (post on-ramp)
- If symptom-free and passing impact prep screens, begin a graded run-walk program around 12–16 weeks postpartum while keeping 2 strength days/week. With autumn 10k as goal, there’s ample time to build volume methodically.

This consolidated plan integrates strength, safe cardio including HIIT-lite, progressive anti-flexion core work, and appropriate postpartum screening so she can train hard enough to feel progress while protecting pelvic floor and core health.

Here’s the full 4-week return-to-fitness on-ramp re-issued with all adjustments layered in: added cardio (including HIIT-lite), the anti-flexion core track, screening/guardrails for diastasis, and the “push” intensity pathway starting mid–Week 2. Assumptions: 10–14 weeks postpartum, OB cleared for moderate exercise, no jumping for 4 more weeks, home setup with light dumbbells/bands. Week 1 is acclimatisation.

Global guidelines
- Frequency targets per week:
  - Strength: 3 sessions
  - Cardio: 2–4 sessions (mix of steady spin/walk and HIIT-lite 1–2x max)
  - Core add-on: 3–4 mini-sessions (8–12 minutes), placed after strength or cardio
  - Impact: none (no running/jumping yet)
- Intensity: most strength work RPE 5–6 (can touch 6–7 on top sets from mid–Week 2). Cardio mostly RPE 4–6; HIIT-lite peaks ≤7.
- Breathing/pressure: exhale on exertion; avoid breath holding. If pelvic heaviness/pressure, leakage, lochia increase, midline coning, or sharp pain, reduce or stop and regress.
- Daily micro (5–8 min all weeks): 3D breathing + pelvic floor connection (5 breaths x 2–3), cat-cow x 6, open books x 6/side, ankle rocks x 10, half-kneeling hip flexor glide x 5/side with glute squeeze.

Screening and monitoring
- Diastasis quick screen: baseline before Week 1, re-check end of Week 2 and Week 4, and spot-check when progressing levers. Track width (finger widths) above/at/below umbilicus, and tension change with exhale/brace. Regress any drill that provokes coning or a soft/sinky response under load.
- Pelvic floor red flags: heaviness/dragging, leakage, increased lochia, pelvic/lumbar pain. If any appear, cut intensity/volume 25–50% that day and retest next session; refer to pelvic health PT if persistent.

Warm-up template (5–7 min before strength or circuits)
- 1–2 min easy march or low step
- T-spine rotation x 6/side
- 10 bodyweight sit-to-stands
- 8 hip hinge wall taps
- 8 wall scap slides

WEEK 1: Acclimatisation (3 strength sessions; 25–35 min; RPE 4–5)
Goal: Rehearse patterns, reconnect breath/core, assess tolerance. Cardio light and seated/low-impact. Core short and supported.

Strength Session A
- Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch with posterior tilt: 30s/side x 2
- Pelvic floor + breath in hook-lying with heel slides: 6–8/side x 2
- Sit-to-stand to high box (BW): 8–10 x 2; 2–3s down
- Incline push-up (hands on counter): 6–8 x 2
- Hip hinge to wall (BW): 8–10 x 2
- Bear hover regress (knees 1–2 cm) on exhales: 5 breaths x 2
- Farmer carry march (very light DBs): 20–30s x 2

Strength Session B
- 90/90 breathing + light band pull-apart: 8 breaths x 2
- Supported split squat (hands to chair as needed): 6/side x 2
- One-arm DB row (supported): 8/side x 2
- Glute bridge (BW, mini pause): 8–10 x 2
- Dead bug arms-only (feet down): 6–8/side x 2
- Tall-kneeling Pallof press (light band): 8/side x 2

Strength Session C
- Low step-up (20–25 cm), slow control: 6/side x 2
- Standing overhead press (very light DBs or band): 6–8 x 2
- RDL pattern with dowel/light DBs: 8 x 2
- Side-lying clamshell: 10/side x 2
- Side plank from knees: 15–20s/side x 2
- Seated calf raise (BW): 10–12 x 2

Cardio Week 1 (pick 2–3)
- Spin/walk steady only, RPE 4–5, 15–25 min.
- Spin example: 5 min easy → 3 x 3 min easy–moderate (RPE 5) with 2 min easy → 5 min cool-down. All seated.

Anti-flexion core add-on Week 1 (2–3x, 8–10 min)
- Dead bug isometric (legs tabletop): 4 x 15–20s with slow exhales (option: hand-to-thigh press)
- Side plank from knees: 2 x 15–20s/side
- Tall-kneeling Pallof press: 2 x 8–10/side (2s hold)
- Quadruped hover regress: 2 x 10–15s
- Optional suitcase hold: 2 x 20–30s/side

WEEK 2: Build base, begin “push” mid-week if green (3 strength sessions; 30–40 min; RPE 5–6, optional top sets ~6–7)
Goal: Slight load/volume bump; introduce light progressions. Start “push” pathway from Session B if symptom-free.

Strength Session A
- Glute bridge with band at knees: 10–12 x 3
- Goblet box squat (light DB): 8–10 x 3
- Incline push-up (slightly lower if clean): 8–10 x 3
- One-arm DB row: 8–10/side x 3
- Dead bug (tabletop with alternating heel taps short lever): 5–6/side x 2
- Farmer carry march: 30–40s x 2–3

Strength Session B (begin push if all green)
- Split squat (light support) → progress to light goblet: 3 x 8–10/side
- DB RDL (2 DBs), 3s eccentric: 3 x 10 (add small load if clean)
- Half-kneeling single-arm press: 8/side x 3
- Tall-kneeling band pulldown or lat prayer: 10–12 x 3
- Pallof press standing: 10/side x 2–3
- Heel-elevated calf raise: 12–15 x 2

Strength Session C (push path continued if green)
- Low step-up with 3s eccentric: 3 x 8–10/side
- Chest-supported DB row: 10 x 3
- Hinge rhythm patterning (no swing): 8 x 2
- Side-lying hip abduction: 10/side x 2–3
- Side plank from knees with top-leg straight: 15–25s/side x 2
- Bird dog (short lever): 6/side x 2

Cardio Week 2
- 3 sessions, 20–30 min.
- Spin: 5 min easy → 4 x 3 min RPE 5–6 seated with 2 min easy → 5 min cool-down.
- Walk: 20–30 min flat/moderate.
- HIIT-lite (add 1 session this week if eager, peaks ≤6.5): Seated spin 60s at RPE 6–6.5 / 90–120s easy x 6 rounds after 8-min warm-up; 5–6 min cool-down.

Anti-flexion core add-on Week 2 (3x, 8–10 min)
- Dead bug contralateral reach (short lever): 2–3 x 5–6/side, 2s pause
- Side plank from knees with top-leg straight: 2 x 20–25s/side
- Standing Pallof press: 2–3 x 8–10/side (add mini step-out on last reps)
- Bear hover holds: 2–3 x 12–20s
- Suitcase carry march: 2 x 30–40s/side or 20–30m/side

WEEK 3: Progressive strength and single-leg control, “push” pathway (3 strength sessions; 35–40 min; RPE up to 6–7 on top sets)
Goal: Add load or reps; more unilateral stability; maintain zero-impact. Cardio includes stronger seated intervals.

Strength Session A
- Goblet squat (to free depth or lower box): 3 x 10–12; last set RPE ~7 if clean
- DB RDL (2 DBs): 3 x 8–10; 3s down + 1s pause at shins; add load if brace clean
- Push-up progression (lowest controlled incline): 3 x 10–12
- One-arm DB row: 3 x 12/side; 1–2s squeeze at top
- Dead bug contralateral reach: 2–3 x 6–8/side
- Suitcase carry: 2 x 30–40m/side

Strength Session B
- Rear-foot supported split squat (rear toes on floor/low pad) with light–moderate goblet: 3 x 8–10/side
- Standing single-arm press: 3 x 8–10/side
- Banded hinge (pull-through or good morning): 3 x 12
- Tall-kneeling face pull (band): 3 x 12–15
- Side plank, top-leg straight: 2 x 25–30s/side
- Pallof step-out: 2 x 8–10/side

Strength Session C
- Step-up (slightly higher if pristine): 3 x 8–10/side, 2–3s down
- Bridge march (pause at top): 3 x 8–10/side
- Chest-supported reverse fly: 3 x 12
- Single-leg calf raise (supported, with DB): 3 x 10–12/side
- Bird dog full: 2 x 8/side
- 4–5 min mobility finisher

Cardio Week 3
- Spin session 1 (tempo blocks): 6 min easy → 3 x 5 min at RPE 6 (seated) with 3 min easy → 5–6 min cool-down (≈30–33 min).
- Spin session 2 (HIIT-lite): 8 min easy with 3 x 20s pick-ups → 6–8 x 60s at RPE 6–7 (seated, 80–95 RPM, moderate resistance) / 90–120s easy → 5–8 min cool-down.
- Optional third steady session: 25–30 min at RPE 5–6.
- Walking can replace or add easy volume 20–30 min on non-strength days.

Anti-flexion core add-on Week 3 (3x, 9–12 min)
- Dead bug with mini band overhead (light pull on exhale): 2–3 x 6–8/side
- Side plank staggered (bottom knee down, top foot planted): 2 x 20–30s/side
- Half-kneeling anti-flexion pressout (hold DB at chest, press out with 2s hold): 2–3 x 8/side
- Bear crawl iso (opposite hand/knee lift 1–2 cm; alternate): 2 x 6–8 slow switches/side
- Offset farmer carry: 2 x 45–60s total, switch at halfway

WEEK 4: Consolidate and prep next phase (3 strength sessions; 35–40 min; RPE 6–7 on top sets)
Goal: Solidify movement quality, small intensity bump, and test tolerance for next block. Still no impact. Intervals stay seated.

Strength Session A
- Goblet squat: 3 x 10–12; add one top set RPE ~7–7.5, then one back-off set (-2 reps)
- DB RDL: 3 x 8–10 heavier; 3s down, slight pause at shins
- Push-up progression: 3 x 10–12 at lowest clean incline
- One-arm DB row: 3 x 12/side; last set AMRAP to technical RPE 8 (leave 2 reps in reserve)
- Dead bug with banded exhale: 2–3 x 6–8/side
- Suitcase carry continuous: 2 x 45–60s total, switch halfway

Strength Session B
- Split squat (moderate goblet): 3 x 10/side
- Hip hinge pulse set: DB RDL to mid-shin + 1–2 “float” pulses each rep: 3 x 8
- Standing single-arm press: 3 x 10/side; final set RPE ~7
- Band pulldown → pull-apart superset: 2–3 rounds of 10 + 12
- Side plank top-leg lift (from knees): 2 x 20–25s/side
- Pallof iso-hold: 2 x 20–25s/side

Strength Session C
- Step-up (highest safe), slow eccentric: 3 x 10/side
- Feet-elevated bridge on low step (add DB on hips if clean): 3 x 8–10
- Chest-supported row + reverse fly combo: 3 x (8 + 10)
- Single-leg calf raise (supported): 3 x 12/side
- Quadruped hover shoulder taps (small range): 2 x 6–8/side
- Finisher: 5–7 min continuous alternating 30s march / 30s suitcase hold (switch sides each round)

Cardio Week 4
- Spin steady day: 10 min easy → 15–20 min continuous RPE 5–6 seated → 5–10 min cool-down (30–40 min total).
- Spin interval day (HIIT-lite): 6–8 min easy → 6 x 2 min at RPE 6–6.5 (seated) with 2 min easy → 6–8 min cool-down.
- Optional third session: 30–40 min walk, mostly flat.
- Keep peaks ≤7; extend duration or add a round rather than increasing intensity.

Anti-flexion core add-on Week 4 (3–4x, 10–12 min)
- Dead bug with heel taps (maintain lumbar neutral): 2–3 x 6–8/side; if coning, revert to Week 3 version
- Side plank from feet supported (top foot in front or knees slightly bent): 2 x 20–30s/side
- Pallof press iso-hold then reps: 2 x 20–25s/side then 6–8 slow presses/side
- Quadruped hover shoulder taps: 2 x 6–8/side
- Suitcase carry continuous: 2 x 45–60s total, switch halfway

Readiness gates and regressions
- Progress a variable (load, reps, ROM, tempo, density, or stability) only if the last session’s variation was symptom‑free and diastasis check shows good tension with exhale/brace.
- If any red flag appears mid-set, stop, reduce ROM/load, elevate support, and coach exhale-to-exert. Retest a lighter version; if still symptomatic, remove that drill for the day.

Nutrition and recovery (non-clinical guidance)
- Protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day across 3–4 meals. Include a protein serving within 1–2 hours post-session.
- Carbs to support energy and milk production if breastfeeding; include a pre-training snack if under-fueled.
- Hydration 2–3 L/day; +500–700 mL around training; more if breastfeeding.
- Sleep: prioritize consistency and naps; if fatigue ≥7/10, reduce day’s volume by 20–30%.

Return-to-running outlook (post on-ramp)
- If symptom-free and passing impact prep screens, begin a graded run-walk program around 12–16 weeks postpartum while keeping 2 strength days/week. With autumn 10k as goal, there’s ample time to build volume methodically.

This consolidated plan integrates strength, safe cardio including HIIT-lite, progressive anti-flexion core work, and appropriate postpartum screening so she can train hard enough to feel progress while protecting pelvic floor and core health.
